subject: Post-demo: hyperscaler gap mapping & 1M token economics
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: hyperscaler gap mapping & 1M token economics

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the benchmark work: 

1) Goal: produce a short gap matrix comparing EdgeScale's current hyperscaler-based inference stack vs Redwood across key unit-econ axes (per-1M tokens cost, P50/P95 latency, batching behavior, and cache hit impact).
2) Test matrix (what we'll run):
   - Synthetic 1M-token workload (mix of short + long prompts) with three batching configs (1, 8, 32) and two context lengths (2k, 8k)
   - Measure: tokens/sec, P50/P95 latency, total tokens billed, and effective per-1M cost using your list-price rates for HyperscalerA/B
   - Cache scenarios: cold start, 50% prefix cache hit, and 90% prefix cache hit (we'll simulate hits using your representative prefix set)
3) Deliverables: CSV of raw metrics, a short PDF gap-matrix with cost reconciliations, and a one-page recommendation on where Redwood gives the most unit-econ upside.

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-gap-plan.pdf (test plan), edgescale_scenario_inputs.csv (please review the prompt mixes)

Proposed timing: run the tests next Tue/Wed (Mar 21–22) if that works for your ops team. We estimate ~4 hours of wall time for the full sweep and will share instrumentation to reproduce.

Ask from you: please confirm (a) which hyperscaler SKUs & NIC/network assumptions we should use for cost calculations, and (b) a procurement contact so we can share a short SOW if needed.

Thanks — happy to hop back on a 30m sync if you prefer.

— Hannah

- Network: assume 25Gbps egress cap — that's our current production config.
- The prompt mixes you attached look representative; please include a small additional subset of long-context chat sessions (4–6 turns) to simulate real product usage.

We can give you a procurement contact for the SOW: procurement@edgescale.com (CC'd). We'll also need an estimate of hours and a breakdown of what the SOW would cover (test runs, analysis, support).

Proposed run window: Mar 21 (UTC) for the synthetic runs.

One ask from our infra lead: can Redwood simulate a prefix-KV cache with configurable hit rates (50%/90%), or do you need us to provide warmed sessions?

Appreciate it — Sarah

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Heads up — technical plan / test-matrix proposal below so we can align on instrumentation before the run. Attaching a quick script (benchmark_script.sh) that we will use as the reference harness.

Test methodology (high-level):
- Workload generation: replay prompts from edgescale_scenario_inputs.csv; mix short (<=64 tokens), medium (~256 tokens) and long (~2k tokens) prompts to hit 1M total tokens per sweep.
- Batch sizes: 1, 8, 32. For each batch config we'll run 3 trials and report median.
- Context lengths: 2k and 8k (model configured accordingly).
- Cache modeling: two options — (A) server-side prefix warming: we pre-inject warmed KV entries using the real prefix set (preferred for accuracy); (B) simulated hit model: after cold run, replay a fraction of prefixes and measure delta. We can support both; Sarah, if you can share the warmed-session list we'll do (A).
- Metrics: tokens/sec, P50/P95 latency, GPU util, memory, and billing tokens (we'll compute effective per-1M token cost by combining runtime duration, actual tokens billed, and your hyperscaler SKU rates).

Instrumentation notes:
- We'll push logs to a shared Drive CSV and a minimal Prometheus scrape for latency histograms.
- Security: runs will be done in Redwood's staging account; no customer data will be uploaded.

Next steps (internal):
1) Finalize edgescale_scenario_inputs.csv with Sarah
2) Prep the staging cluster and confirm NIC config (25Gbps)
3) Run sweep on Mar 21 and produce raw CSV + gap-matrix PDF by Mar 22 EOD

Jordan — can you prep a short SOW + hours estimate for procurement? I'll sync infra to reserve GPU time.

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
